summary: Game crashes/freezes after creating/entering a Superflat world without presets
description: When create a superflat world without presets, it crashes. 1.16.2-pre2 Description: Ticking player java.lang.IllegalStateException: Unregistered biome at bw.b(SourceFile:88) at java.base/java.util.Optional.orElseThrow(Optional.java:385) at bw.a(SourceFile:88) at bw.a(SourceFile:68) at bx$a.a(SourceFile:55) at bx.a(SourceFile:31) at ck.a(SourceFile:62) at bx.a(SourceFile:31) at aah.v_(SourceFile:484) at aay.b(SourceFile:207) at nd.a(SourceFile:234) at aax.c(SourceFile:173) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.b(SourceFile:881) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.a(SourceFile:810) at emy.a(SourceFile:92) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.w(SourceFile:669) at net.minecraft.server.MinecraftServer.a(SourceFile:254) at java.base/java.lang.Thread.run(Thread.java:844) 1.16.2-pre3 [18:07:58] [Render thread/WARN]: Received invalid biome id: -1
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Launch Minecraft.  
2. From the Main menu select **Singleplayer** and click **Create New World**.  
3. Click **More World Options**, then set **World Type** to **Superflat**.  
4. Leave the preset field unchanged (do not click **Customize** or select any preset).  
5. Click **Create New World** to generate the world.  
6. Observe that the game crashes or freezes, and the log shows an error such as `java.lang.IllegalStateException: Unregistered biome` or `Received invalid biome id: -1`.
Environment: Minecraft Java Edition Versions: 1.16.2 Pre-release 2, 1.16.2 Pre-release 3
Observed Behavior: When a player creates a Superflat world without selecting a preset the game immediately aborts the loading process. In version 1.16.2‑pre2 the server thread throws an IllegalStateException reporting an unregistered biome and the stack trace shows calls through bw.b, bw.a, bx$a.a, bx.a, ck.a, aah.v_, aay.b, nd.a, aax.c, MinecraftServer.b, MinecraftServer.a, emy.a, MinecraftServer.w and finally the Java thread runner. In the later 1.16.2‑pre3 build the same situation does not produce a crash but instead the render thread repeatedly logs a warning that an invalid biome id –1 was received, causing the client to freeze in a loop of messages. The underlying cause is that the default Superflat preset string contains the literal “null” for the biome entry, which is not a valid biome identifier; the game attempts to resolve this entry, fails to find a matching biome, and consequently either throws the exception or enters an infinite warning loop. The problem occurs only when no explicit preset is chosen; selecting any preset such as Classic Flat avoids the failure.
Expected Behavior: When a player creates a Superflat world and leaves the preset field empty, the game should automatically fall back to a valid default or other appropriate preset (such as Classic Flat) that includes a proper biome, generate the world, and allow the player to enter without any crashes, freezes, or error messages about an invalid biome ID.
